thread.title: Broadcom (AVGO) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Broadcom (AVGO) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo Shares of Broadcom ( AVGO ) have been under the pressure ever since the semiconductor giant warned of weak demand for its wireless chips back in April.
The downbeat commentary spooked investors even more after management lowered the top end of the company’s previously issued revenue forecast for the just-ended quarter. The company forecasted revenue of $4.975 billion to $5.025 billion, down from previously forecasted net revenue of $5 billion (give or take $75 million). Well — that is now coming to a head as Broadcom is set to report second quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Thursday.
It would seem, however, that the company’s dominance in the mobile chip industry, where it provides wireless components to Apple’s ( AAPL ) iPhones, among others, will remain a growth catalyst — and then some — for the foreseeable future. Wall Street expect the San Jose, Calif.-based company to earn $4.76 per share, up 29% year over year, on revenue of $5.01 billion, up 19%. For the full year, earnings are projected to rise 21.7% year over year to $19.49 per share, while full-year revenue of $20.8 billion would rise 17.7% year over year.
Broadcom stock has been one of the high-flyers among the chip sector over the past couple of years, soaring 90% since 2015, compared to an 32% rise in the S&P 500 Index. The company’s extensive product portfolio, which serves multiple applications, including wired infrastructure, wireless communications and enterprise storage continue to be high-growth revenue streams — all of which are growing at double-digit rates.
What’s more, the company’s relationship with Apple could still be underestimated, according J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur. In a research note to investors Tuesday, Sur outlined how Broadcom’s close ties with Apple can help Broadcom — by virtue of being the sole provider of chips designed to enable wireless charging, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GPS capabilities in new iPhones — generate $10 in revenue for each iPhone sold .
"We believe Broadcom will maintain 100 percent share (non-radio frequency chipsets) on 2018 iPhone models with its dominant position as the premier connectivity (WiFi/Bluetooth/GPS) chipset supplier and its close partnership with Apple on analog interface and wireless charging," Sur said. While citing the potential strength of revenue growth, profitability and free cash flow, Sur reiterated his Overweight rating and $337 price target.
From Wednesday’s close of $263.52, the price target implies potential premium of 28%. So, for investors with a long-term horizon of 12 to 18 months, buying Broadcom ahead of Thursday’s results seems like a smart move, especially with the shares still down from its 2018 high of $285 and up just 2% year-to-date.
